# Ignition, distributor and misfires

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Locate, remove, swap, and reinstall the distributor while marking rotor orientation. [t2124]

[Partial] Remove the old distributor and install a new or re-manufactured one with firm torquing. [t2124]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Locate the distributor on top of the engine.
2. Disconnect the negative battery terminal to prevent sparks or electrical noise.
3. Remove the two screws holding down the distributor cap using a flathead screwdriver.
4. Mark one or two lines on the distributor housing and extend them to a static point on the engine block that is not part of the distributor itself.
5. Mark the orientation direction of the rotor inside the distributor housing, treating it like clock positions.
6. Remove any stiff black intake hoses located at the 5 o'clock position from the distributor if extra workspace is needed.
7. Unscrew the bolt securing the distributor using a screwdriver or a socket with an extension and universal joint.
8. Pull the old distributor straight up by its housing, allowing the rotor to spin clockwise as it lifts out.
9. Spin the pinion gear on the bottom of the new distributor to rotate the internal rotor into position.
10. [Partial] Mark the new distributor's screw holes and rotor orientation exactly like the old one was marked.
11. Insert the bolt back in place while holding the new distributor housing steady against any spinning resistance.
12. [Partial] Push the new distributor down until it seats, ensuring the rotor marks align with the static engine mark.
13. [Partial] Reinstall the distributor cap if not included with the unit and tighten its two screws.
14. Connect all spark plug wires that click into place on the cap terminals.
15. [Partial] Reattach any other fittings such as intake lines or battery connections removed earlier.
16. [Partial] Start the engine to verify operation before proceeding to timing checks.

_Procedure reported by [t2124]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-distributor-replacement.5695/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t2124] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the old distributor.
2. [Partial] Install a new or re-manufactured distributor in its place.

</details>

## Tips & gotchas

- Marking the spark plug wires is optional but helps avoid swapping them one by one. [t2124]
- Take time to mark lines on both the distributor housing and a static engine point for alignment reference. [t2124]
